clusters.name: Language Disorder (F80.2)
items: Reduced vocabulary (DSM p.47)
Limited sentence structure (DSM p.47)
Impairments in discourse (DSM p.47)

clusters.name: Speech Sound Disorder (F80.0)
items: Persistent difficulty with speech sound production interfering with speech intelligibility (DSM p.50)

clusters.name: Childhood-Onset Fluency Disorder / Stuttering (F80.81)
items: Sound and syllable repetitions (DSM p.51)
Sound prolongations of consonants and vowels (DSM p.51)
Broken words, audible or silent blocking (DSM p.52)
Circumlocutions, excess physical tension, monosyllabic whole-word repetitions (DSM p.52)

clusters.name: Social (Pragmatic) Communication Disorder (F80.82)
items: Deficits in using communication for social purposes (DSM p.54)
Impairment changing communication to match context or listener (DSM p.54)
Difficulties following rules for conversation and storytelling (DSM p.54)
Difficulties understanding nonliteral/ambiguous language and inferences (DSM p.54)

criteria.thresholds: Onset in early developmental period; quantifiable impairment in social, academic, or occupational functioning (DSM p.48, 50, 52, 55)

epidemiology.prevalence: 7.4% of elementary school children for Language Disorder (Dulcan p.161); ~1% for Stuttering (DSM p.52)
epidemiology.sex_ratio: Language: 8% boys vs 6% girls (Dulcan p.161); Speech Sound: 1.5-1.8:1 M:F (DSM p.50); Stuttering: M > F (DSM p.52)
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: 2-6 years for Stuttering (DSM p.52); >=4-5 years for SPCD (DSM p.55, Dulcan p.163)
epidemiology.heritability: Substantial heritability for Language Disorder and Stuttering (DSM p.49, 53)
comorbidities: ADHD (65% boys, 57% girls with written language deficits) (Dulcan p.162)
Specific Learning Disorder (80% reading problems) (Dulcan p.161)
epidemiology.prognosis: 65%-85% recovery rate in Stuttering (DSM p.53); Receptive Language Disorder carries poorer prognosis (DSM p.48)

etiology.genetic: FOXP2 mutation, 22q11.2 deletion, 4 specific stuttering genes, >3x risk in 1st degree relatives (DSM p.51, 53, Dulcan p.177)
etiology.neurobiology: CSTC circuits, Glutamate master switch, Dopamine Go/Stop motor loops (StahlNeuro p.87, 95)
etiology.environmental: Bilingualism does not cause or worsen disorder; stress exacerbates stuttering (DSM p.48, 52)

items: TILLS (Test of Integrated Language and Literacy Skills) ages 6-18 (Dulcan p.162)
CASL-2 (Comprehensive Assessment of Spoken Language-2) ages 7-18 (Dulcan p.165)
CCC (Children's Communication Checklist) (Dulcan p.165)
SLDT-E:NU (Social Language Development Test-Elementary) ages 6-12 (Dulcan p.162)
CAPS (Clinical Assessment of Pragmatics) ages 7-18 (Dulcan p.162)
Language Use Inventory (Dulcan p.165)
key_numbers: 1 in 12 children (8%) affected by communication disorders (Dulcan p.158)
50% speech intelligible at age 2, mostly intelligible at age 3, 100% by age 5 (DSM p.50-51)
8 late-acquired speech sounds ('Late Eight') normal up to age 8 (DSM p.51)

first_line: SLP Therapy focused on Morphosyntax and vocabulary (Dulcan p.162)
Enhanced Milieu Teaching (EMT) 28 parent sessions (Dulcan p.163)
Fluency Shaping and Stuttering Modification (Dulcan p.160)
second_line: IEP under IDEA or 504 Plan accommodations (Dulcan p.158)
Methylphenidate or Amphetamine for comorbid ADHD (StahlKids p.31, 324)
Guanfacine ER for comorbid ADHD/impulsivity (StahlKids p.252)
key_side_effects: Nonspeech oral-motor exercises are INEFFECTIVE for Speech Sound Disorder (Dulcan p.159-160)
Insomnia and reduced appetite from stimulants (StahlKids p.31, 324)
Sedation and hypotension from Guanfacine (StahlKids p.252)
treatment.monitoring: Monitor speech intelligibility, reading comprehension at grade 4+, and ADHD/anxiety comorbidities (Dulcan p.161-162)

items: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD): Distinguished from SPCD by presence of Restricted, Repetitive Behaviors (RRBs) (DSM p.55, 66)
Intellectual Developmental Disorder (IDD): Language deficit must exceed nonverbal cognitive level (DSM p.49, 56)
Selective Mutism: Mute in specific social settings, normal speech at home (DSM p.51, 222-223)
Social Anxiety Disorder: Normal social communication skills acquired but unexpressed due to fear (DSM p.55)
Dysarthria: Neurological motor signs and altered voice quality (DSM p.51)
key_numbers: 0 RRBs in SPCD history or present; >=2 RRBs required for ASD (DSM p.55, 56-57)
3x risk of sexual assault in adult females with childhood language disorder (DSM p.48)
80% of children with language disorder develop reading problems (Dulcan p.161)

high_yield: Presence of past or present Restricted/Repetitive Behaviors (RRBs) mandates ASD diagnosis, superseding SPCD (DSM p.55, 66).
Stuttering has a 65%-85% recovery rate; severity at age 8 predicts persistence into adolescence/adulthood (DSM p.53).
Nonspeech oral-motor exercises are explicitly NOT evidence-based for Speech Sound Disorder (Dulcan p.159-160).
Receptive language impairment carries a worse prognosis and higher reading comprehension failure rate than expressive-only impairment (DSM p.48, Dulcan p.161).
Language Disorder prevalence is 7.4% in elementary children, with 80% developing reading comprehension deficits by grade 4 (Dulcan p.161).
